transcript:
(Meeting header)
Date: 2027-01-12
Start: 15:00 PST
End: 15:47 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO, Helios), Sofia Alvarez (ML Lead), Ravi Patel (Product), Elaine Chu (Security)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on POC gates: define success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy), agree on workload sizing and sample dataset, set benchmark plan and timeline (kickoff, access setup, midpoint review, exec readout). Security/SSO and VPC peering flagged as early blockers.

Topics Covered:
- Success criteria definition (p95 latency, cost target, accuracy thresholds)
- Workload characterization (avg tokens, qps, peak windows)
- Benchmark plan (synthetic and replay runs, dataset redaction)
- Timeline and milestones (kickoff -> setup -> midpoint -> exec readout)
- Security & access (VPC, SSO, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Marcus Lee: Good, thanks. We've got a few folks here — Sofia, Ravi and Elaine are on, too. Appreciate you taking time.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi all. Quick agenda: align on what constitutes success for the POC, understand your workload shape, go over a benchmark plan and then agree on timeline and access. 
[00:23] Sofia Alvarez: Sounds good. For context, we're trying to move our triage assistant from a prototype to a production inference path. Daily active users ~ 120k, peak concurrency around 300 QPS for the assistant, average prompt length 120 tokens and average completion 260 tokens. There's some burstiness at 10am-11am and 2pm-3pm PST.
[00:41] Ravi Patel: Right, and product wants p95 latency under 600ms for chat completions and cost not to exceed $0.015 per 1k tokens equivalent — that's their loose target.
[00:51] Marcus Lee: Security is a must — we need VPC peering or private link, SOC 2 type II, and KMS integration for keys. Elaine's on the call to speak to that.
[01:01] Elaine Chu: Yep, we'll need to review the security questionnaire. Also data residency — some PII may remain in logs if not redacted. We'll need log redaction guidance and audit log retention settings.
[01:12] Jordan Kim: Great, that's precisely the things we want to lock down. Priya, do you want to start on the benchmark/throughput side?
[01:17] Priya Nair: Sure. Based on the numbers Sofia gave — 300 QPS peak, avg request ~380 tokens total — we should plan benchmark runs at 1x, 2x, and 3x the observed peak to understand headroom. We'll run three kinds of tests: synthetic short + long tails, replay of anonymized traces, and an end-to-end app simulation with cold-starts to capture KV cache effects.
[01:38] Sofia Alvarez: When you say 3x, that's mostly for understanding degradation, right? We won't run that in prod, but want to see how graceful degradation looks.
[01:45] Priya Nair: Exactly. The POC will capture throughput curves, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and token/sec for cost modeling. We'll also test quantized variants to get a cost/latency tradeoff.
[01:55] Marcus Lee: Can you give a rough expected instance count or GPU sizing so I can get internal approvals? We can't provision blindly.
[02:02] Priya Nair: Based on similar customers, for a 300 QPS peak at ~380 tokens, if you use a 8-GPU pod (A100 equivalent), with continuous batching we estimate baseline p95 around 350-450ms for FP16 model. For int8 quantized variants that might drop to 250-350ms and reduce token cost by ~40%. That's a rough number — we'll tighten it after we see sample workloads.
[02:23] Ravi Patel: Ok that's useful. For success criteria let's write these down: p95 latency < 600ms, end-to-end accuracy drop < 2% compared to current model, and cost per 1k tokens < $0.015. Are those acceptable guardrails?
[02:36] Marcus Lee: Looks fair as initial POC gates, but product would like a higher bar on latency if possible. Maybe p95 < 500ms as a stretch goal.
[02:44] Jordan Kim: We'll capture both baseline target and stretch target in the benchmark doc and flag where tradeoffs exist.
[02:50] Elaine Chu: Also, from security, telemetry and audit logs need to be retained for 1 year and KMS must be customer-managed in dedicated/private setups.
[02:58] Priya Nair: That's doable. For hosted POC we can offer customer-managed keys via our KMS integration and show audit logs. For private/dedicated we'll provide full KMS control.
[03:08] Sofia Alvarez: What about data redaction? We can't ship raw logs with PII offsite.
[03:13] Priya Nair: We'll run redaction in two layers: client-side scrub where possible and server-side rules in the replay harness. We'll send a redaction checklist but we need a sample of typical prompts to validate the rules.
[03:24] Marcus Lee: We'll anonymize and provide a 100k request sample dataset. Can Redwood host the replay or should we run locally?
[03:30] Jordan Kim: Both options. For speed we usually run the replay in Redwood's sandbox under strict access controls. If policy forbids, we can run the harness in your VPC and we'll send the containerized runner.
[03:42] Priya Nair: For the benchmark plan, deliverables will be: (1) benchmark spreadsheet with metrics and thresholds; (2) replay harness + redaction runbook; (3) performance report with cost model; (4) exec readout slide deck.
[03:55] Ravi Patel: Timeline wise what's realistic? Product wants exec readout to align with the Feb leadership meeting on 2027-02-22.
[04:03] Jordan Kim: That gives us about six weeks. Proposed milestones: Kickoff this week (we're on the kickoff), Access and dataset provision by 2027-01-20, Initial bench runs and tuning by 2027-02-04, Midpoint review week of 2027-02-08, Final runs and report by 2027-02-18, Exec readout 2027-02-22. Does that work?
[04:23] Marcus Lee: That's aggressive but doable if we prioritize access.
[04:27] Elaine Chu: Access gating — VPC peering and security questionnaire answers are blockers. We'll aim to provide the answers by 2027-01-17 and start conversation on peering immediately.
[04:37] Priya Nair: For access checklist we'll need: SSH keys for runners or S3 access for dataset, service account for logs, and optionally VPC peering config. Jordan will send a concrete checklist.
[04:47] Jordan Kim: I'll send the checklist today and the benchmark template by Friday.
[04:51] Sofia Alvarez: A few technical clarifications: Which model family do you recommend? We're currently on an open LLM similar to Llama 2 7B for the prototype.
[04:59] Priya Nair: We'll propose two candidate profiles: a cost-optimized 7B quantized variant and a latency-optimized 13B FP16 variant. For your prompt size the 7B quantized often hits the cost goals but may degrade on some worst-case accuracy metrics; we'll present delta metrics.
[05:14] Marcus Lee: Are there any known caveats around KV cache or streaming? We rely on partial streaming responses in the UI.
[05:20] Priya Nair: We support streaming and KV cache in the runtime but behavior depends on deployment mode. In hosted mode streaming latency is usually lower because of our edge routing. For private/dedicated, network topology matters — we'll include tracing hooks in the run.
[05:33] Ravi Patel: For the mid-point review, what should we prepare from our side?
[05:36] Jordan Kim: Please have: (1) anonymized dataset sample uploaded, (2) list of success criteria with priority (must have/ stretch), (3) any compliance constraints. We'll present initial numbers and tuning recommendations.
[05:48] Priya Nair: A note on benchmarks — there will be transcription noise in token counts across tokenizers; we'll normalize with a shared tokenizer and document tokenization differences.
[05:58] Sofia Alvarez: Good point. Also we need cost modeling per 1k tokens including caching effects; otherwise numbers will mislead.
[06:06] Priya Nair: We'll include a baseline that shows cost with and without prefix/KV caching and a run that simulates warm cache.
[06:14] Marcus Lee: If we see accuracy regressions beyond the 2% threshold, what's the rollback? Will you recommend model variant adjustments or configuration changes?
[06:22] Priya Nair: We'll triage by prompt subsets — some prompts are sensitive to quantization; we'll recommend using a mixed model strategy: low-latency quantized for common prompts and FP16 for critical prompts. Redwood supports routing by policy so we can set that up in the POC.
[06:38] Elaine Chu: On the security side: audit logs, encryption at rest, and SSO integration are must haves. We also want to ensure that any temporary credentials are rotated and not stored in long-lived logs.
[06:49] Jordan Kim: Noted. We'll include short runbook for credentials lifecycle during the POC.
[06:54] Sofia Alvarez: Is there a recommended cadence for check-ins? Weekly or biweekly?
[06:58] Jordan Kim: Weekly syncs work well for fast POCs — 30 minutes. Midpoint review will be a longer 60-minute readout.
[07:05] Marcus Lee: Ok, locking weekly 30m on Mondays, midpoint week of 2027-02-08 and exec readout 2027-02-22.
[07:12] Ravi Patel: Anything else on blockers?
[07:15] Elaine Chu: We need the security questionnaire and a data flow diagram from Redwood.
[07:19] Priya Nair: We'll attach both in the follow-up email; the data flow diagram will include options for hosted vs private.
[07:25] Jordan Kim: Great. Quick recap of next steps — I'll send the benchmark template and access checklist; Priya will send sizing recommendations; Helios will provide sample dataset and security answers. We'll schedule the weekly cadence and midpoint.
[07:39] Marcus Lee: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:42] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks, appreciate it.
[07:44] Jordan Kim: Thanks, talk soon.

(End of meeting)

Notes: Minor transcription errors expected — e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed 'K V cash' and 'VPC peering' sometimes as 'VPC pairing'. Links shared: benchmark template (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/helios-template), security questionnaire (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/q_helios), replay harness repo (link: https://github.com/redwood/poс-replay-runner)
